column1: Binding affinity at the mouse μ-opioid receptor (mMOR) was measured by assessing displacement of a radiolabeled ligand in membrane preparations derived from CHO cells expressing the mouse μ-opioid receptor. Membranes were exposed to increasing concentrations of test compounds and incubated for 1.5 h with radioligand to compete for receptor binding, with nonspecific binding defined in the presence of 5 μM naltrexone. Bound radioligand was quantified following filtration and radiometric detection, and compound activity was determined from dose–response relationships.

Activation of the human nociceptin/orphanin FQ (NOP) receptor was measured by assessing agonist-induced intracellular calcium mobilization in CHO cells stably coexpressing human NOP and the chimeric Gαqi5 protein. Cells were loaded with the calcium-sensitive fluorescent dye Fluo-4 AM and exposed to increasing concentrations of test compounds. Intracellular calcium levels were quantified by measuring fluorescence changes, and compound activity was determined from concentration–response relationships.

Antinociception mediated non-selectively at opioid receptors was assessed in male CD1 mice using the acetic acid–induced writhing test. Animals received subcutaneous administration of test compounds, and the number of writhes was counted over a 10-min observation period following intraperitoneal injection of 0.6% acetic acid. Compound activity was determined from dose–response relationships.

Binding affinity at the kappa opioid receptor (KOR) was measured by assessing displacement of the radiolabeled ligand [3H]-diprenorphine in membrane preparations derived from CHO cells expressing KOR. Membranes were exposed to increasing concentrations of test peptidomimetics and incubated for 1 h to allow binding to reach equilibrium. Bound radioligand was quantified following filtration and liquid scintillation counting, and compound activity was determined from concentration–response relationships.

Activation of the μ-opioid receptor (MOR) was measured by assessing agonist-stimulated G protein signaling through [35S]GTPgammaS binding in membrane preparations expressing MOR, with DAMGO as the reference agonist. Membranes were exposed to increasing concentrations of test peptidomimetics in the presence of GDP and incubated for 1 h to allow nucleotide exchange. Receptor-stimulated [35S]GTPgammaS binding was quantified by measuring radioligand incorporation following vacuum filtration, and compound activity was determined from concentration–response relationships.

Antinociception mediated non-selectively at opioid receptors was assessed in mice using the warm-water tail-withdrawal test. Animals received intraperitoneal administration of test compounds using a cumulative dosing procedure, and tail-withdrawal latency was measured following immersion of the tail in a 50 °C water bath with a 20-s cutoff. Compound activity was determined from dose–response relationships.
